articles.title: Asia, Africa to drive expansion of India's export markets as shipments grow across regions
articles.desc: India's merchandise exports have shown strong growth, particularly in Africa and Asia, according to recent government data. Exports to Africa increased by 44 percent, while shipments to Asia surpassed USD 100 billion. Engineering goods, electronic goods, and petroleum products have driven this expansion significantly. Notable growth was observed in markets such as Tanzania and Kenya in Africa.

articles.title: South Korea prepares market stabilisation funds after KOSPI hits 10-month low
articles.desc: In response to falling stock indices, South Korea's finance ministry is poised to activate market stabilisation funds. The KOSPI index has plummeted, marking its lowest point in the last ten months. An emergency meeting was convened by the finance minister to explore strategies for restoring investor confidence. Among the discussed actions are temporary regulations on stock buyback limits for publicly listed companies.

articles.title: Chinese national Li Ming charged in fraud case in Singapore linked to Megaspeed and Alice Huang: Report
articles.desc: Li Ming, a Chinese national, is facing fraud charges in Singapore regarding alleged transshipment of Nvidia chips. He was involved with Megaspeed, a company linked to Alice Huang, the former romantic partner of Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang. Li is accused of misleading an American supplier by misrepresenting the intended destination of purchased servers. Following an investigation, Megaspeed was placed on a no sell list by Nvidia.

articles.title: Crude oil futures brace for OPEC+ output decision amid supply glut concerns: Analysts
articles.desc: Next week promises to be a rollercoaster for crude oil futures as the OPEC+ meeting approaches. Traders are keeping a close eye on supply insights from the American Petroleum Institute and Energy Information Administration. Trading will be quiet on Tuesday due to Guru Nanak Jayanti. While concerns about a global supply surplus loom large, they overshadow geopolitical tensions in West Asia.

articles.title: Rising government debt unlikely to trigger broad sovereign crisis in 2027: UBS
articles.desc: Government borrowing and debt-servicing costs are likely to escalate challenges for major economies by 2027. UBS reports that pressure stems from refinanced debt from low interest rates previously. Factors contributing to public finance pressure include ageing populations and entitlement spending. Measures like bond buybacks and changes in debt issuance strategies can help manage financing pressures. Nonetheless, UBS warns about potential difficulties that could lead to a debt crisis.

articles.title: Why gold’s five-year winning streak is under threat after dramatic selloff
articles.desc: Gold has fallen to around $3,510 an ounce after hitting a record $5,594.82 earlier in 2026, putting it on track for its first annual loss in five years. A stronger dollar, elevated bond yields, profit-booking and weaker safe-haven demand continue to pressure prices.

articles.title: Italian jeweller and businessman Paolo Bulgari dies aged 89
articles.desc: In a statement to Italian media, his family remember him as "the greatest jeweller of our time".

articles.title: InvIT IPO rush gathers pace; 4-5 private trusts likely to go public by Mar 2027
articles.desc: Four to five Infrastructure Investment Trusts are expected to launch public offerings to raise Rs 17,000 crore by 2027. These offerings aim to mobilise long-term capital for infrastructure development while appealing to a broader pool of investors. Notable companies like Brookfield and Investcorp are preparing to shift to public InvITs. In the past, InvITs raised around Rs 88,000 crore, demonstrating investor appetite.

articles.title: 5 penny stocks plunge up to 68% in six months. Do you own any?
articles.desc: Five BSE Smallcap penny stocks have fallen between 21% and 68% in recent months. Kalind and Empower India led the declines, plunging 68% and 62%, respectively.

articles.title: Government, corporate spending to sustain global growth in 2027 as inflation eases: JPMorgan
articles.desc: Global economic growth is projected to be resilient in 2027 due to continued government investment and corporate spending. Investment in technology and recovery in consumer demand are expected to drive this growth forward. Corporate investment, especially in artificial intelligence, is noteworthy, with major firms planning significant expenditure. Inflation pressures are anticipated to ease, strengthening household spending. However, rising government borrowing and competition for capital may pose challenges for financial markets.

articles.title: Reliance Brands FY26 revenue up 3.8% to Rs 3,390.9 crore; loss narrows to Rs 137 crore
articles.desc: Reliance Brands has marked a significant financial milestone, achieving a revenue of Rs 3,390.89 crore for FY26 and reducing losses. Operating more than 1,085 Points of Sale nationwide, the brand continues to collaborate with over 90 partner names. Recent acquisitions, including Hamleys and new entries like Stella McCartney and Fabletics, demonstrate the company’s drive to lead in the competitive fashion and lifestyle industry.

articles.title: Anthropic's post-debut stumble delivers reality check for AI trade
articles.desc: Anthropic’s shares fell about 9% after their market debut, deepening concerns over stretched AI valuations and showing that even a marquee listing has not revived investor enthusiasm for the sector. The focus is now shifting to whether Anthropic can justify its roughly 40-times-sales valuation and whether a potential OpenAI IPO next year can restore appetite for AI stocks.
